brief.scope: Independently review only the corrected trailing-newline test and its custody against the supplied failed implementation report, prior test approval, correction evidence and task contract. Do not edit tracked files. Reproduce the original contradiction using ordinary strings and verify the successor preserves the exact positive assertion plus a discriminating negative check. Exercise a correct renderer and the untrimmed faulty counterparty. Re-run test_job_outputs*.py and the existing task suite where allowed, confirming no other frozen file changes. Return exact refs, disposition, approve/changes and executable receipts/limits. This is test acceptance only, not approval of the unaccepted source patch.

envelope.note:
REVIEW — model claude-opus-5 (Opus 5), ref 43cd8b59ea43228c4b83c282b43c4c9ae1cc41f9 against 710dbac38c3b187eb4b3302308430c0a6dec4d76. Verdict: approve for test acceptance only (0 p1, 0 p2, 1 p3, 2 opinions). Scope held to the corrected trailing-newline test and its custody. No tracked file was read-modified; git status --porcelain is empty. Everything I wrote lives under this dispatch's out/. Full receipts in out/receipts.md.

Refs. Reviewed commit 43cd8b5, tree 97faff29b14b76cb918f9a48a86ff8cee63ba166, committer GPT-6 <noreply@openai.com>. Prior approved test freeze 026fcad433aab03d802e98063b5d9a4a67e759ba. render.py blob 7b3d21cc -> 4b3b6d1e. The supplied context/diff.patch is byte-identical to git diff 710dbac..43cd8b5 (diff -q, no output); git diff --check on the range is empty.

Contract premise, measured not paraphrased. ops/devlane/task/CONTRACT.md:385-386 declares "After removing trailing CR/LF from the rendered native prompt, before any appended envelope schema, append two LFs and `Declared job outputs:` followed by LF." The producer's restatement is exact.

The contradiction, reproduced with ordinary strings. For prompt "Write the skeptic report.\n\n", PROMPT.rstrip("\r\n") + "\n\n" == PROMPT, so the contracted exact result is PROMPT + CHECK_TESTS_SECTION and startswith(PROMPT) is necessarily True. out/control_reviewer_trailing_lfs.py (9 tests, OK) proves the old pair is unsatisfiable by any renderer, subTesting a correct one, an untrimmed one and one that drops the two LFs — all three fail the old assertFalse. I did not stop at plain strings: out/control_reviewer_old_file.py drives the byte-for-byte pre-correction blob 7b3d21cc (extracted with git show into out/render_at_026fcad.py) against a correct renderer, and the trailing-LFs case is the sole failure of the five, its traceback naming assertFalse. The contradiction was in the approved file itself, not in a restatement of it.

The successor. Line 196-199, assertEqual(got, "Write the skeptic report." + "\n\n" + CHECK_TESTS_SECTION), is unchanged byte for byte — the positive assertion is preserved exactly. Line 200-203 replaces assertFalse(got.startswith(prompt)) with assertFalse(got.startswith(prompt + "\n"), "unstripped trailing newlines remain before the two LFs"). Four lines added, one removed, nothing else in the file.

Both counterparties exercised against the landed test, not a copy of it. out/control_reviewer_live_append.py imports ops/devlane/task/tests/test_job_outputs_render.py unmodified and swaps only outputs_support.envelope in memory (3 tests, OK): a correct renderer passes all 5 AppendDeclaredOutputsToPrompt cases with 0 failures and 0 errors — the old file could not do this; the untrimmed renderer (prompt + "\n\n" + section) is caught on the trailing-LFs case; the absent seam leaves it red with no collection error. Combined reviewer controls: python3 -m unittest discover -s <out> -p 'control_reviewer_*.py' — Ran 15, OK. The producer's own in/control_faulty_trailing_lfs.py also runs green here (4 tests, OK), independently of mine.

Suites. python3 -m unittest discover -s ops/devlane/task/tests -p 'test_job_outputs*.py' — Ran 99, FAILED (failures=95), 0 errors; per file test_job_outputs.py 60, test_job_outputs_accept.py 17, test_job_outputs_render.py 18. python3 -m unittest discover -s ops/devlane/task/tests -p 'test_*.py' — Ran 312, FAILED (failures=95), 0 errors, so 312-99=213 pre-existing task tests all green. These are the prior review's counts at 026fcad unchanged, which is the point: the correction flipped nothing green and bought nothing. Isolating with -k trailing_lfs shows the case failing at line 196, the equality, "AssertionError: '' != 'Write the skeptic report.\n\n...'" — red on the absent seam, never on the negative. ruff check on the file: All checks passed.

Custody. git diff --name-status 026fcad..43cd8b5 is three paths: the two dispatch records and test_job_outputs_render.py. sha256 at 43cd8b5 for outputs_support.py 2ac0b7ed..., test_job_outputs.py e2eb943a..., test_job_outputs_accept.py dd2cbc3a..., fixtures/job_outputs/duplicate-path-member.json 6786a977... are identical to the same paths at 026fcad; jobs.json is 6e0479fb..., the brief template sha, unchanged. render.py is 8adcd884..., matching record 6e070c. ops/devlane/task/envelope.py appears nowhere in the 710dbac..43cd8b5 range and still exports no append_declared_outputs, load_outputs, outputs_from_job, render_declared_outputs, validate_outputs, OUTPUTS_SCHEMA or TRANSPORT_RESERVED, so the tests remain red against an absent API and could not have been tuned to a live implementation. The two committed records are byte-identical to the supplied inputs (38eaf862..., 25ddf396...).

Opinion 1, not chargeable. The corrected negative has no marginal detection power where it sits. Once line 196's assertEqual passes, got IS the exact string, and EXACT.startswith(prompt + "\n") is a constant False; when line 196 fails, line 200 is never reached. So no renderer output can pass the equality and fail the negative. I measured this rather than asserting it. It is not a defect: the sibling test_trailing_crlf_is_stripped has the identical shape (assertEqual then assertNotIn("\r")), so this is the file's existing idiom, the ruling asked for a negative, and the check is genuinely discriminating in isolation — it separates the untrimmed renderer from the correct one. It documents the charge; the equality does the detecting. A later pass wanting real marginal power would have to drop the equality, which would be worse.

Opinion 2, custody, not chargeable. GPT-6 — the producer of the unaccepted envelope.py at record 20260906T111156Z-code-codex-ba1209, whose implementation these tests judge — carries a Co-Authored-By trailer on this test-correction commit. The branch convention credits a finding's originator that way: 026fcad, a2fb2a6 and 57d265a all carry Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 for the reviewer who raised the finding. Two things keep the producer firewall intact in substance. No Reviewed-by: GPT-6 trailer was added, so no approval is claimed (the earlier three do carry Reviewed-by: Claude Opus 5). And the edit was made by Grok 4.6 under record 6e070c, the original test author, with the positive assertion byte-identical, no test flipped green and the case still red. The risk the firewall guards — an implementer relaxing a test to admit its own code — did not materialise and is measurable as not having done so.

Limits, declared not inferred. bash ops/bin/suites.sh was refused by this profile (Bash(bash ops/bin/*) is not on the allowlist), so the lane-wide green question is unanswered here, not answered negatively. python3 -V was refused by the compound-command guard, so nothing is stamped to an interpreter version — UNRESOLVED. envelope.py was read only for its public-name list, to prove absence; the unaccepted source patch from ba1209 was not read, applied or evaluated, and this approval says nothing about it. The faulty and correct counterparties are stubs I wrote — no candidate append_declared_outputs exists at this ref to exercise. The p3 below is a record-pointer defect, not a test defect.

Freeze readiness: yes for the corrected test. The contradiction is proven and removed, the exact positive assertion is preserved byte for byte, a discriminating negative for unstripped trailing newlines is present, the four other append cases and every other frozen artifact are untouched, and the suite is still red against the absent API it must drive.
